chunks: O children of Israel, We delivered you from your enemy, and made a covenant with you on the right side of the Mount, and sent down for you manna and quails,

key_terms.السَّلْوَى: Quails (a type of bird sent as food)
key_terms.الْمَنَ: Manna (a sweet substance sent from heaven)

ai.seo_question: What are the three main blessings God mentions to the Children of Israel in Surah Taa-Haa?
ai.summary: In Surah Taa-Haa, this verse highlights God's historical grace toward the Children of Israel, specifically emphasizing the covenant established at the 'right side' of Mount Sinai, which Shia exegesis often interprets as a place of divine acceptance and spiritual elevation. The mention of Manna and Quail serves not only as a physical provision but also as a sign of divine sustenance during their wilderness journey, reinforcing the theme of reliance on God amidst trials.
